j.brief_text: We run three independent coffee shops in Bristol. Should we launch a loyalty app, open a fourth shop in Clifton, or start selling our beans wholesale to offices? Our goal is to raise monthly profit from about £18,000 today to at least £24,000 within nine months. The loyalty app would cost about £400 a month, a fourth shop would need around £120,000 of fit-out, and wholesale would need a part-time salesperson at £1,500 a month.

conversation_turns.assistant_message:
I’ve mapped the three routes plus carrying on as now. Your stated goal is **at least £24,000 monthly profit**, from about **£18,000 today**; the nine-month deadline is retained, though this model cannot yet test timing directly.

A provisional first pass exists only to expose assumptions, not to answer the choice. The key unknowns are each route’s profit uplift, demand uptake, and the Clifton funding cost.

I’ve read your goal, ‘monthly profit’, as the total across every tier, including ‘Loyalty app monthly gross profit’, ‘Clifton monthly operating profit’ and ‘Wholesale monthly gross profit’. If you meant only part of it, say which.

The model was saved.

Your results are ready. You can view them now or ask me to explain them.

No figure is set for "Commercial uptake shortfall" yet, so the analysis treats it as zero. How likely or how large is it today?

This comparison uses Olumi’s estimates for "Loyalty app deployment", "Loyalty app monthly cost", "Clifton shop opening", "Clifton fit-out spend", "Monthly fit-out financing cost", "Wholesale salespeople", "Wholesale salesperson monthly cost". These are factor starting values on the comparison’s paths. Other model assumptions may also affect the result.

‘Launch loyalty app’: between less than 1% and 18% chance of meeting your goal, in this model. Of the links not sized yet, it depends most on how strongly ‘Loyalty app deployment’ affects ‘Loyalty app monthly gross profit’, which isn’t sized in the model yet. ‘Open Clifton shop’: between about 11% and 62% chance of meeting your goal, in this model. Of the links not sized yet, it depends most on how strongly ‘Wholesale salespeople’ affects ‘Wholesale monthly gross profit’, which isn’t sized in the model yet.

**The comparison is provisional, not a settled choice.** In this model, 43% of runs supported ‘Open Clifton shop’, on assumptions including Olumi’s starting estimates; small assumption changes could alter that ordering. That share is not its chance of meeting your target.

- Olumi supplied 24 values behind the comparison, rather than you.
- Commercial uptake shortfall was missing and treated as zero—not evidence that demand will meet expectations.
- This result does not establish reaching **at least £24,000/month within nine months**.
